principles: Make the operator action explicit and auditable.
Prefer fresh bounded worker context over hidden inherited conversation state.
Do not widen authority, receipt, merge, or DONE semantics for dispatch follow-up work.
drivers: A completed worker needs a second assignment path that can set the worker role.
Full-history fork is not required and currently prevents role selection.
Existing dispatch metadata already has most of the needed pack/prompt/worktree machinery.

options.name: A: Extend dispatch_resume to accept new role/objective
pros: Reuses an existing verb users may know
cons: Confuses rerun/resume of the same dispatch with assigning a new follow-up task
Harder to preserve original dispatch metadata and create clear lineage
Existing dispatch_resume intentionally means same bounded metadata

options.name: B: Add dispatch_reassign that creates a fresh follow-up dispatch linked to the completed one
pros: Matches the user model: assign new work after completion
Can set role/objective/instructions without mutating the old dispatch
Uses parentDispatchId lineage and fresh prompt/worktree metadata
Keeps full-history fork out of the critical path
cons: Adds one new command and policy/fact registrations
Needs focused help text and smoke coverage

options.name: C: Document manual dispatch_prepare workaround only
cons: Does not solve the ergonomic pitfall
Still leaves users guessing how to restart under worker role

chosen: B: Add dispatch_reassign that creates a fresh follow-up dispatch linked to the completed one
rationale: The user wants to assign more work after a worker finishes, not simply rerun the same dispatch. A new dispatch_reassign command can read the prior dispatch, require explicit follow-up instructions, create fresh role-aware prompt metadata, set parentDispatchId to the prior dispatch, and clearly state that this is summary/instruction continuity rather than full-history inheritance.

preMortem.scenario: The command accidentally mutates or reruns the original dispatch instead of creating a follow-up dispatch.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation reuses dispatch_resume or writes over the old dispatch id.
preMortem.consequence: The prior worker evidence and receipt lineage become ambiguous.
preMortem.mitigation: Create a new dispatch id by default, store parentDispatchId as the previous dispatch id, and add smoke assertions for old/new ids.

preMortem.scenario: The worker still cannot tell which role it should use.
preMortem.trigger: Role remains only in pack JSON and not visible in prompt/status text.
preMortem.consequence: The follow-up launch behaves like a generic worker and repeats the reported pitfall.
preMortem.mitigation: Render role/objective/continuity mode in prompt and reassign output; assert prompt text includes requested role.

preMortem.scenario: The new path overclaims memory continuity or authority.
preMortem.trigger: Output implies inherited history or accepted receipt from the previous worker.
preMortem.consequence: Operators may trust stale or hidden context as evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Use fresh-context wording, carry only explicit prior summary/instructions, and preserve authorityChanged=false, receiptVerified=false, productionDone=false in result types.
